A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BRAF V600 mutations are present in hairy cell leukemia, but not in most other lymphoid neoplasms, including other splenic marginal zone B-cell lymphomas.
we have developed a simple and cost-effective method to screen patients with hairy cell leukemias and related disorders for BRAF mutations that can be used by most laboratories.
BRAF mutations are not limited to patients with hairy cell leukemias.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BRAF V600 mutations are present in all cases of hairy cell leukemia.
we have shown that the BRAF V 600E mutation is a disease defining feature of hairy cell leukemia.
we have found a new method for detecting the BRAF V 600 E mutation in hairy cell leukaemia.
